\[
s_k = \begin{cases} +1 & n_k \ge c + t \\ 0 & \lvert n_k - c \rvert < t \\ -1 & n_k \le c - t \end{cases},
\qquad
U = \sum_{k=0}^{7} [s_k = +1]\, 2^k,
\qquad
L = \sum_{k=0}^{7} [s_k = -1]\, 2^k,
\qquad
t = 5
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(c\): The center pixel
- \(n_k\): The neighbor at 45 k degrees, counterclockwise from the right
- \(t\): The threshold
- \(U, L\): The upper and lower codes

A local binary pattern sets a bit for every neighbor at least as bright as the center, so in a flat, noisy area noise alone decides the bits. Tan and Triggs added a dead band of width t: a neighbor within t of the center counts as 0, neither brighter nor darker. The ternary code has 3^8 values, too many for a histogram, so it is split into two binary codes. The upper code U has a bit for each neighbor that is clearly brighter, and the lower code L for each that is clearly darker. Bit k belongs to the neighbor at 45 k degrees, counterclockwise from the right. With t = 0, the upper code is the local binary pattern of the 8 neighbors.
